messages.subject: Non-comp estimation
parts:
Hi Phil,
I`m interest in 2 dimensional non-compensatory model. I want to constrain a par for item 1-3 for first dim., and item 4-6 for second dim. I can generate data myself and your packages` simdata function. But when I estimated both of data sets they have bad estimation first 6 items. I tried many ways but results not satisfied. Not constrained dim. a par. is very high(~3.5-9) or very low(~.1-.7) for first 6 items. Can you explain my problem?

Thanks,
Levent.

Codes:
n=20000
item=20
a=matrix(2,item,2)
b=matrix(rnorm(item*2),item,2)
a[1:3,1]=0
a[4:6,2]=0
d=a*-b
sigma=matrix(c(1,0,0,1),2,2) 
theta=matrix(round(mvrnorm(n,c(0,0),sigma),3),ncol=2)
pn=matrix(0,n,item)
for (i in 1:3)
  pn[,i]=1/(1+exp(-1*(a[i,2]*theta[,2]+d[i,2])))
for (i in 4:6)
  pn[,i]=1/(1+exp(-1*(a[i,1]*theta[,1]+d[i,1])))
for (i in 7:item)
pn[,i]=(1/(1+exp(-1*(a[i,1]*theta[,1]+d[i,1]))))*
       (1/(1+exp(-1*(a[i,2]*theta[,2]+d[i,2]))))
datan=matrix((pn>runif(n*item,0,1))*1,n,item)
model <- mirt.model('F1=4-20
                    F2=1-3,7-20')
datn=mirt(datan,model,itemtype = "PC2PL",TOL=.001)
coef(datn)
sim=simdata(a,d,n,itemtype='partcomp',sigma=sigma,Theta=theta)
simn=mirt(sim,model,itemtype = "PC2PL",TOL=.001)
coef(simn)

Items 1-6 look like they should be 2PL models, not partially compensatory. These models are not nested (think about how the parameters should look for the PC2PL to reduce to the 2PL.....you realize that the intercept has to be Inf for this to really occur), so if you want these as 2PL you need to change the itemtype input to a suitable vector of types. 

Phil

simn=mirt(sim,model,itemtype = "PC2PL",TOL=.001)

Hi Phil,

Thanks for respond. You are right. I don`t have problem constained (a=0) items now.

But I have seen a problem in non-compensatory data generation. I generate 2 dimensional data compensatory and non-compensatory data includes 33 items and first 24 constrained a=0, for  n=10,000. Actually for non-comp. generate 2 data sets, one of using your simdata functions other one using compare uniform dis. (0,1) with examiners probabilities. 

When I generate 10 times these 3 datasets and then estimate: In compensatory model average absolute difference of theta between gen. and est. around .20-.21 always. But non-comp. models estimations: in with your functions 5 of 10 absolute difference between gen. and est .36-.37 and other  5 of 10 were .28. In with manual gen. 3 of 10 absolute difference between gen. and est .40-.45 and other  7 of 10 were .21-.22. And if average absolute difference of theta is higher also item paremeters are unstable and bad.

I think difference between non-comp models your function and my manual generation (.28 in yours  .21 in mine) because of I use D=1.7 in gen. But I didn`t understand why non-comp. parameters unstable and bad while comp. model is stable? Is it wrong my expectation about stabilization? 

If you run codes a few times you can understand me well.

n=10000
library(mirt)
library(MASS)
sigma=matrix(c(1,0,0,1),2,2) 
theta=matrix(round(mvrnorm(n,c(0,0),sigma),3),ncol=2)
item=33
model=mirt.model('F1=1-12, 25-33
                 F2=13-33')
b=matrix(0,item,2)
b[1:12,1]=-1:1
b[13:33,2]=-1:1
b[25:33,1]=rep(-1:1,each=3)
d=matrix(0,item,3)
pc=matrix(0,n,item)
pn=matrix(0,n,item)
a=matrix(2,item,2)
a[1:12,2]=0
a[13:24,1]=0
d[,1:2]=-1*a*b
d[,3]=d[,1]+d[,2]
for (i in 1:item) {
  pc[,i]=(1/(1+exp(-1.7*(a[i,1]*theta[,1]+a[i,2]*theta[,2]+d[i,3]))))
  if (a[i,1]==0 | a[i,2]==0 )pn[,i]= pc[,i]
  else pn[,i]=(1/(1+exp(-1.7*(a[i,1]*theta[,1]+d[i,1]))))*(1/(1+exp(-1.7*(a[i,2]*theta[,2]+d[i,2]))))
}
datac=matrix((pc>runif(n*item,0,1))*1,n,item)
datan=matrix((pn>runif(n*item,0,1))*1,n,item)
e=matrix(NA,item,2)
e[1:24,1]=d[1:24,3]
e[25:item,1:2]=d[25:item,1:2]
datan1=matrix(simdata(a,e,n,itemtype=c(rep("dich",24),rep("partcomp",9)),Theta=theta),n,item)
datc=mirt(datac,model,itemtype = '2PL')
datn=mirt(datan,model,itemtype = c(rep("2PL",24),rep("PC2PL",9)))
datn1=mirt(datan1,model,itemtype = c(rep("2PL",24),rep("PC2PL",9)))
mean(abs(theta-fscores(datc, full.scores=T)))
mean(abs(theta-fscores(datn, full.scores=T)))
mean(abs(theta-fscores(datn1, full.scores=T)))

#Thanks

messages.subject: Re: Non-comp estimation
parts:
Have you considered plotting your response curves before simulating data from them? To me they look rather extreme and localized entirely in one sharply discriminating response quadrant, so it's not uprising the recovery is poor (the recovery will generally be poor anyway due to parameter exchangeability; see my APM article relating to estimating these models). 

To get an idea of the shapes, try using the shiny plotting GUI to see what response surface looks reasonable.

library(mirt)
itemplot(shiny=TRUE)
# change to partcomp class, and check multidimensional
# move slides to match your model, and compare what happens when you modify parameters even a little 

Phil
